The must-sees

12 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Building · 1924

    Chilehaus

    Fritz Höger designed it for a merchant who had made his fortune in Chile, and it was finished in 1924. It is the best-known building of the Kontorhaus district, listed by UNESCO with the Speicherstadt.

    Look for

    The street Fischertwiete runs right through the building under tall arches.

  2. 02
    Culture · 2017

    Elbphilharmonie

    Herzog & de Meuron set the glass building on top of the old Kaispeicher A warehouse. It opened in January 2017, and the public Plaza wraps around it with views over the harbour.

    Look for

    Ride the long escalator up from the entrance. It curves, so from the bottom you can’t see where it ends.

  3. 03
    Civic building · 1897

    Hamburg City Hall

    Finished in 1897 after the old town hall was lost in the Great Fire of 1842. Both the Senate and the city parliament, the Bürgerschaft, still meet here.

    Look for

    Walk through to the inner courtyard and find the Hygieia Fountain, which remembers the cholera epidemic of 1892.

  4. 04
    Museum · 1869

    Hamburger Kunsthalle

    It opened in 1869 and has grown into three connected buildings. The collection runs from medieval altarpieces to Caspar David Friedrich and contemporary art.

    Look for

    Find Caspar David Friedrich’s Wanderer above the Sea of Fog: a man seen from behind on a rock, looking over the mist.

  5. 05
    Waterfront

    Jungfernstieg

    It follows the line of the medieval mill dam that turned the Alster river into lakes. Alster boats still leave from the landing stage here.

    Look for

    Across the water, the Lombard and Kennedy bridges divide the Inner Alster from the much larger Outer Alster.

  6. 06
    Museum · 2001

    Miniatur Wunderland

    Two brothers opened it in 2001 and have kept adding new countries ever since. Tiny trains, planes and cars run through scenes where day turns to night every few minutes.

    Look for

    In the airport section, model planes taxi along the runway, take off and land.

  7. 07
    Station · 1911

    Old Elbe Tunnel

    Opened in 1911 so dock workers could reach the shipyards on the south bank. Pedestrians and cyclists can still walk through it to Steinwerder for a view back at the city.

    Look for

    Along the tiled walls, find small ceramic reliefs of fish, crabs and other creatures of the river.

  8. 08
    Venue

    Reeperbahn

    The name comes from the rope makers who once worked here. In the early 1960s the Beatles played club after club around the Reeperbahn, years before their first hit.

    Look for

    On Beatles-Platz, at the corner of Große Freiheit, steel outlines of the band stand on a round black disc like a record.

  9. 09
    Neighbourhood

    Speicherstadt

    Built from the 1880s on oak piles for the free port, it is the world’s largest historic warehouse district. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015.

    Look for

    Look up at the gables: many still carry a winch beam, used to haul sacks of coffee and spices straight up from the barges.

  10. 10
    Church · 1912

    St. Michael’s Church

    The church burned in 1906 and was rebuilt to the old design by 1912. For generations sailors used its tower as a landmark when coming up the Elbe.

    Look for

    The tower clock has the largest face of any church clock in Germany, about eight metres across.

  11. 11
    Church · 1874

    St. Nicholas Memorial

    When its tower was completed in 1874 it was briefly the tallest building in the world. The church was destroyed in the air raids of 1943 and now remembers the victims of war and persecution.

    Look for

    A glass lift inside the ruined tower carries visitors to a viewing platform about 76 metres up.

  12. 12
    Waterfront

    St. Pauli Piers

    The present building went up in the early 20th century as the terminal for ocean steamers. Today the floating pontoons are the starting point for harbour tours and city ferries.

    Look for

    Moored by the piers, the Rickmer Rickmers, a green-hulled three-masted sailing ship, is now a museum.
